newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso ends strong on inflows.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso ends strong on inflows.

text.p: The Philippine peso finished strong on Tuesday at 26.371 to the dollar from 26.373, helped by inflows of arbitrage money, traders said.
"A lot of swaps were done in the one, two and three months," a foreign bank dealer said.
After T-bill rates softened in the auction, investors decided to invest in the peso before rates slipped further, she added.

T-bill rates have risen in the past month as the Central Bank quelled speculation against the peso by raising its overnight borrowing rate. The speculation was brought on by fears of capital flight from stock market divestments.
But last Thursday, the Central Bank cut its rate by 0.25 percentage points to 11.25 percent.
"It seems we're on the way to normalcy because the stock market is stabilising," Central Bank Treasurer Sergio Edeza said.
Due to the inflows, traders said the Central Bank may have bought $20 to $65 million at various rates from 26.371/26.372. Market volume was $164.5 million from $131 million.
